summary: The Recycling Infrastructure and Accessibility Act of 2025 directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to establish a competitive pilot grant program to improve recycling accessibility in underserved communities using a hub-and-spoke model.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to apply for and receive competitive grant funding ranging from $500,000 to $15,000,000 to improve local recycling infrastructure.
affected_groups.group: States, local governments, Indian Tribes, and public-private partnerships

affected_groups.effect: Receive prioritized focus and at least 70 percent of set-aside program funds to improve local recycling access, transport, and collection capacity.

key_provisions: Establishes the Recycling Infrastructure and Accessibility Program within 18 months of enactment to award competitive grants to eligible entities.
Sets grant amounts between $500,000 and $15,000,000, with the Federal share capped at 90 percent unless waived due to significant financial hardship.
Requires that at least 70 percent of available funds be set aside for projects in a single underserved community or multiple underserved communities.

Allows grant funds to be used for increasing transfer stations, expanding curbside recycling collection, and leveraging public-private partnerships, while explicitly prohibiting funds for recycling education programs.
Authorizes appropriations of $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029.

Requires the Administrator to submit a report to Congress detailing program implementation, grant recipients, actions taken, and improvements in recycling rates two years after the first grant is awarded.
missing_information: Total cost of the program beyond the authorized appropriations of $30 million annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
Specific demographic or economic thresholds that define an underserved community beyond the text's description of lack of access or processing capacity.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Recycling Infrastructure and Accessibility Act of 2025 directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to establish a competitive pilot grant program to improve recycling accessibility in underserved communities using a hub-and-spoke model.
summary_detail.significance: This bill creates a federally funded grant program administered by the EPA dedicated to investing up to $30 million annually through fiscal year 2029 into recycling infrastructure, transfer stations, and curbside collection systems specifically targeted at underserved regions.
